chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Daybali told us, saying: Abu Abdullah told us, saying: Sufyan narrated, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

There is no envy except in two cases: A man to whom God has granted wealth, and he spends it during the night and during the day; and a man to whom God has granted the Quran, and he recites it during the night and during the day.

key_terms.حَسَد: Envy or jealousy (admiration of a blessing in another)
key_terms.يَقُومُ بِهِ: He stands to recite/pray with it (referring to Quran recitation)

ai.seo_question: What are the two conditions under which envy is considered permissible in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to distinguish between destructive envy (hasad) and virtuous admiration (ghibtah), a key concept in Shia ethics. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) limits legitimate envy to two specific domains: material wealth spent in charity and the Quran mastered through consistent recitation and practice. This highlights the Shia emphasis on both spiritual devotion and practical generosity as the primary measures of a believer's excellence.
